reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) directly supports all key premises: it confirms the deposition method, the specific Al content, the dual-phase oxide composition, the denser oxide layer, and the ~75% reduction in oxide scale thickness under relevant conditions. The conflicting evidence (E3, E4) discusses Cr coatings, not AlNbTiZr, and does not contradict these premises.
premises: AlNbTiZr MEA coatings can be deposited on Zr-alloy substrates by RF magnetron co-sputtering
A coating with ~10.2 at.% Al forms a dual-phase oxide scale of Nb2Zr6O17 and ZrO2
This dual-phase oxide scale is denser and reduces oxygen penetration compared to uncoated substrate
The 10.2 at.% Al coating reduces oxide scale thickness by ~75% (from ~3.36 μm to ~0.84 μm) in autoclave tests
The coating acts as an effective oxygen barrier under high-temperature pressurized water conditions
